title: Exact claim meaning
obligation: The checker must know the required guarantees, including mandatory UB freedom; producers cannot select their own success criterion.

title: Compilation-subject identity
obligation: Evidence must bind to source, dependencies, target, features, effective configuration, and other relevant compilation inputs.

title: Faithful parsing and elaboration
obligation: An accepted AST or IR must correspond to the selected source; checking a producer-supplied AST alone leaves that connection trusted.

title: Generated-code coverage
obligation: Macro expansion, generated functions, and implicit operations must participate in the claim rather than disappear behind source-level annotation scanning.

title: Typing and entry-state validity
obligation: Rust typing and valid incoming state must be justified or explicitly assumed without assuming the implementation’s own safety.

title: Caller-domain adequacy
obligation: A safe API cannot acquire hidden soundness preconditions. Restricted decoders and ghosts must not silently exclude permitted callers.

title: Executable-dependency coverage
obligation: Calls, dispatch, callbacks, destructors, cleanup, and relevant external operations must be covered or explicitly bounded.

title: Faithful lowering
obligation: Every transformation must preserve the observations and safety conditions required by the claim.

title: Exposure of source UB
obligation: Correspondence must retain or reconstruct obligations preceding source UB, including when the result is discarded.

title: Execution-path coverage
obligation: Proofs must cover the relevant nondeterministic choices and outcomes, not merely successful returns or explored traces.

title: Progress correspondence
obligation: Erased steps must not hide divergence when a termination claim depends on them.

title: Scalar correctness
obligation: Machine bounds, overflow modes, unchecked arithmetic, shifts, and conversions require adequate interpretations.

title: Layout and ABI correspondence
obligation: Mathematical sizes and alignments must correspond to the actual Rust types and target; a supplied descriptor is not that evidence.

title: Representation validity
obligation: Initializedness, padding, invalid values, niches, pointer-bearing bytes, and typed transfers must remain represented where relevant.

title: Memory-access authority
obligation: Bounds must compose with allocation lifetime, provenance, alignment, permissions, borrowing, and aliasing.

title: Ownership transitions
obligation: Projection, mutation, write-back, transmutation, and consumption must preserve surviving capabilities and destruction obligations.

title: Initialization and cleanup
obligation: Partial initialization, dropping, unwinding, cancellation, and restoration require explicit semantics.

title: Type and trait invariants
obligation: All relevant mutations and implementations must preserve the laws consumed by generic proofs.

title: Concurrent behavior
obligation: Interference, weak memory, synchronization, spawned execution, and reclamation need corresponding semantics and coverage.

title: External behavior
obligation: FFI, I/O, hardware access, and environmental effects need explicit contracts or interpretations.

title: Specification adequacy
obligation: Accepted contracts must establish the required property; vacuous domains and weakened goals must not substitute for it.

title: Logical validity and assumptions
obligation: Check proof terms, referenced definitions, imported dependencies, and the exact permitted assumptions.

title: Composition and artifact applicability
obligation: The checked relationships must compose over the same subjects and definitions; cached evidence needs a justified reuse rule.

title: Acceptance and publication
obligation: Missing stages, tool failures, development modes, stale inputs, or incomplete work cannot construct an ordinary successful result.
